title: 2026-01-15-sdk-integration-walkthrough-caldera-finance
summary: AE + SE walked through Redwood SDK quickstarts (Python + TypeScript), auth patterns (API key, SSO), env setup, and demoed a minimal integration. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, latency/cost knobs, and security needs. Agreed next steps: send quickstart repo, security docs, and schedule POC benchmark run.
transcript: 00:00 Sarah Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll get started in a minute, nice to meet you all. 00:06 Tom Rivers: hey Sarah, thanks, we're excited to see the SDK flow. 00:12 Miguel Ortiz: hi team miguel here from redwood, i'll go through the code samples and python and ts quickstarts. 00:17 Lina Patel: great, we've been evaluating a couple of providers - our main concerns are latency for inference and data residency, also SSO for the console. 00:28 Sarah Chen: perfect, we'll cover all that. quick agenda: auth and env setup, python and ts quickstarts, then a short demo of the console optimize recommendations, and q&a. 00:40 Miguel Ortiz: first up, the simplest way to auth is api key - set REDWOOD_API_KEY on your ci/cd or local env. in python it's pip install redwood-inference and then from redwood import Client, client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) - you can also pass region. 00:56 Jamal Ahmed: when you say region, do you mean hosted region? can we pin requests to eu-west? 01:03 Miguel Ortiz: yes you can pass region="eu-west-1" or use a per-tenant config, if you're on dedicated we can pin capacity in a specific region or on-prem. 01:15 Renee Cho: for security, do you support sso or sso-enabled console access? we need SAML with okta. 01:22 Sarah Chen: yes we support SAML/SSO for the console, and you can map roles with RBAC. for api-level auth we support api keys and we've got a roadmap for short-lived tokens and workspace-scoped keys. 01:34 Tom Rivers: do keys rotate automatically? do you have KMS integration? 01:38 Priya Rao: we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for private deployments and support envelope encryption for hosted - you can also use our rotation APIs or integrate with your secret manager. 01:49 Miguel Ortiz: quick note on the ts sdk, npm i @redwood/inference, then import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); you call client.generate({ model: 'rwd-small-v2', input: '...' }) 02:06 Lina Patel: rwd-small-v2 - how does that compare to other models? 02:10 Miguel Ortiz: rwd-small-v2 is our optimized open model variant, we also have rwd-large and quantized flavors for lower cost. i'll send a model performance sheet after this. 02:19 Jamal Ahmed: any special config for streaming? we need partial tokens in our app. 02:23 Miguel Ortiz: yes streaming is supported in both SDKs, python uses client.stream_generate(...) and ts supports async iterator pattern. small caveat: streaming on dedicated can be tuned for latency vs throughput. 02:37 Sarah Chen: let's show the quickstart repo - so here's the link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (shared) 02:44 Miguel Ortiz: in the python quickstart there's a minimal flask example that calls the sdk, sets REDWOOD_API_KEY, and a small local cache for prefix tokens. note the code comments about batching config. 02:58 Tom Rivers: can we run this behind our internal api gateway? cors? tokens? 03:02 Miguel Ortiz: yes standard, we recommend server-side calls or a short-lived session token if you need browser clients. 03:12 Renee Cho: what's your retention policy for logs, and can we disable storing raw requests? 03:17 Sarah Chen: by default hosted keeps logs for X days but we have customer-configurable retention on enterprise plans and we can disable storing inputs for regulated customers; audit logs are retained and available via the console. we'll share the SOC2 and security pack. 03:31 Lina Patel: for the POC we want to test with our real prompts and measure 99th percentile latency at 256 tokens, cost per 1k tokens, and memory usage. 03:40 Sarah Chen: good criteria - we usually recommend trying a small pilot on dedicated for predictable p99, but you can start hosted then scale to dedicated. 03:50 Miguel Ortiz: for benchmarking, send us a sample payload set and i'll run a latency run on our dev fleet and share numbers; if you'd like we can spin a dedicate test pool for a short run. 04:02 Jamal Ahmed: what's the onboarding timeline typically? 04:06 Sarah Chen: self-serve takes minutes for hosted; dedicated POC provisioning is typically 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and procurement. 04:14 Tom Rivers: procurement and legal - any standard terms? 04:17 Sarah Chen: we have an enterprise SLA addendum and security questionnaires we can send, and a standard msa; our legal team will work with you. 04:27 Lina Patel: in the code we saw env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, do you have examples for rotating keys in CI? 04:32 Priya Rao: we include a sample k8s secret manifest and a github actions step in the repo. also show an example of using the workspace-token pattern for ephemeral sessions. 04:44 Jamal Ahmed: any pitfalls integrating embeddings? we plan to use embeddings for semantic search; we have a vector db already. 04:50 Miguel Ortiz: embeddings are exposed in both sdks, we return vector arrays and a ids field. we recommend normalizing and using our optional dedupe cache for repeated calls. 04:59 Tom Rivers: do you have a migration path from openai api calls? 05:03 Miguel Ortiz: yes we provide a small adapter layer in the quickstarts to map common parameters, though some model names and behaviors vary. 05:11 Sarah Chen: ok let's recap and next steps. 05:14 Sarah Chen: action items: miguel will run benchmark, i'll send quickstarts and security docs, lina will provide prompts. 05:22 Miguel Ortiz: any other q's? 05:24 Tom Rivers: not for now. thanks! 05:27 Sarah Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and schedule the POC kickoff. 05:33 Speaker 6: (inaudible)
